analyst_view.overall: Early view: Galatasaray host Rizespor four days after the Besiktas derby and four days before the Champions League trip to AEK Athens, so rotation is likely. One report expects Rafael Leao back for this game while others say his strain could keep him out for up to six matches, and Victor Osimhen's return from knee surgery should be close by then. Rizespor (11th) have scored only 13 goals and are without Can Bozdogan.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.8 goals. Galatasaray beat Konyaspor 4-0 and Amed 4-3 in their last two league games and Osimhen may be back, but rotation between the derby and AEK, and Rizespor's low-scoring games (29 goals in eleven), keep me on the number rather than above it.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.9 corners, mostly Galatasaray's. Against a deep Rizespor that fits; the only doubt is how many first-choice wide players Okan Buruk uses between two big games.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.2 cards and I lean lower. Galatasaray were not booked at all in their last home game against Amed, and against a deep-lying side the cards are more likely to come from Rizespor chasing the ball than from the hosts.

shots.text: The numbers say 31.6 shots. Galatasaray will create a lot at home even with changes, as they did with 17 shots against a far stronger Amed side, so I stay near the number.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.7 shots on target. Aleksey Batrakov's form and a possible Osimhen return support it, while rotation pulls the other way, so I keep it close to the number.
